description: This Radio World article reports the FCC's notice of proposed rulemaking on improving the reliability and resiliency of communications networks during disasters and on better situational awareness afterwards. The proposal, which cites Hurricane Ida's damage on the Gulf Coast in late August 2021, asks whether participation in the Disaster Information Reporting System (DIRS), used by broadcasters and other providers to report outages, should become mandatory, and asks detailed questions on how backup power can be deployed to cut power-related service disruptions. It raises the possibility of backup power requirements for participants in DIRS and the Network Outage Reporting System, a list that includes broadcasters, which could bring costs for stations without backup power at their transmission sites. Producer: trade publication Radio World, dated 5 October 2021, reporting FCC action. Coverage: United States. Access: free web page. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: it is a news summary of a proposal, not the FCC text or its final rules, and the outcome of the rulemaking is not covered. Simulation uses: it documents a policy scenario for backup power and outage reporting in broadcast resilience and emergency-response studies. Related records: none linked.
